title: Pinned release handshake and performance declaration for onboarding v2 models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a formal contract and publishable artifact that defines the backward-compatibility guarantees, parameter surface, prompt format version, and the canonical performance profile for onboarding and pinning any v2 family model into the Redwood catalog. This ticket produces the 'Pinned Release Handshake & Performance Declaration' artifact used by PM, RD (runtime), QA, and Console to validate and publish a pinned model version.
background: We onboarded multiple v2-family models in pilot. Engineering and PM observed small parameter aliasing and output-shape drift between upstream checkpoints and our optimized serving paths (quantized kernels, KV caching). Customers who pin versions expect deterministic behavior for prompts + parameter contracts. We need a readable, executable contract and an automated verification harness that ensures new pinned versions meet both semantic stability and the published performance profile before being eligible for 'pinned' promotion.
proposed_contract: The contract is a single-line human-readable declaration plus machine-checkable artifacts: (1) prompt-format version (PFv), (2) canonical parameter surface and alias map, (3) output shape schema (JSON Schema string), (4) performance profile matrix (latency/throughput/cost/memory for canonical workloads), (5) regression harness links and thresholds, (6) allowed graceful-degradation behaviors (fallbacks), (7) mandatory rollout checklist. The contract must be signed by Runtime, QA, and PM and published in the catalog entry for the pinned version.
performance_profile: Canonical workloads: short-chat (max_tokens=64, seq_in=32), long-generation (max_tokens=1024, seq_in=512), embeddings-encode (batch=32, seq=128). Metrics (hosted mode, n1-standard GPU equivalent): short-chat: p50=28ms, p95=62ms, p99=120ms; long-generation: p50=180ms/token, p95=420ms/token; embeddings-encode: throughput=620 items/sec (batch 32). Cost guidance: ~USD 0.45 per 1k tokens (attn + softmax optimized path). Memory steam: working set 14.3 GiB after KV warm-up. Recommended batch size for serving 4-16 for interactive, 32-64 for offline batch. KV-cache warm-hit target >85% after 10 distinct requests per session. Quantization guidance: int8-lora compatible, small accuracy delta (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) < 0.02.
parameter_surface_and_aliasing: Supported runtime parameters: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop (list), seed (optional for deterministic CI), logit_bias (map), presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, return_full_text (boolean), output_format (enum: text|json|tokens). Aliasing map: temp -> temperature (deprecated but accepted), length -> max_tokens (accepted but warns), format -> output_format (maps legacy 'json_v1' to 'json'). Disallowed: arbitrary callback hooks or custom kernel toggles exposed to customers. Any change to parameter names must have an alias and backwards compatibility shim and be documented in the contract.
prompt_format: Define PFv1 and PFv2 example snippets. PFv1 (legacy): single string prompt. PFv2 (canonical): list-of-turns chat object with metadata: [{role: 'system', content: '...'}, {role: 'user', content: '...'}]. For pinned v2 models we require PFv2 canonicalization at the API layer: legacy inputs are normalized to PFv2 using deterministic rules. The contract includes a canonicalizer with unit tests and examples showing edge cases (embedded JSON, trailing whitespace, multiple stop tokens).
output_shape: Canonical outputs for 'json' output_format are validated against an inline JSON Schema that requires: top-level 'id' (string), 'choices' (array of objects with 'index' (int) and 'message' (object with 'role' and 'content')), and optional 'usage' token counts. The contract forbids changing the structure (field names/types) for pinned versions. Non-conforming outputs cause an automatic regression failure with a clear error report.
onboarding_tests: unit: canonicalizer_roundtrip_test (200 sample prompts across PFv1->PFv2 conversions)
integration: param_alias_acceptance_test (verify alias mapping for 50 parameter combos)
regression: semantic-stability-suite (1k eval prompts, semantic similarity >= 0.92 vs reference)
perf: perf-matrix CI (short-chat, long-generation, embeddings) run in perf lab with p95 gating thresholds
acceptance_criteria: All onboarding_tests pass in CI on the optimized runtime image
Semantic-stability-suite: mean cosine similarity >= 0.92 and no more than 2% of samples with catastrophic shift (different intent classification)
Performance: p95 latency must be within 15% of published performance_profile for short-chat and embeddings; long-generation per-token time within 20%
Output schema conformance: 100% for 'json' output_format on sampled prompts
Signed contract file (artifact) checked into runtime's onboarding bucket and referenced by catalog entry
Documentation for aliases and prompt canonicalization published and linked from the Console UI
rollout_plan: 1) Register candidate pinned version in staging catalog with 'pinned: candidate' flag. 2) Run automated onboarding_tests in staging GPU pool. 3) If tests pass, schedule a canary in hosted with 1% traffic and dedicated logging + tracing. 4) After 48 hours and no regressions, escalate to 10% then 25% over 1 week. 5) Once stable at 25% for 72h, flip to 'pinned: active' and publish in catalog. All steps are gated by CI artifacts and runtime perf baselines.
rollback_plan: Immediate automatic rollback on detection of any of: (A) semantic-stability-suite failure post-deploy, (B) p95 latency regression > 2x of baseline, (C) output-schema violation (any), or (D) elevated error-rate (5xx) above 0.5% in canary window. Rollback steps: set route to previous pinned binary, revoke new catalog tag, notify stakeholders via #runtime-ops and open an incident ticket referencing this ENG key.
